analytics.label: Base rate of yoy(revenue)[t] > 50% among filers with revenue of at least $100.00B

inputs.label: Revenue: every filer's row, by the first concept that has one

analytics.reading: Among filers with revenue of at least $100.00B (the company left out), yoy(revenue)[t] > 50% held in 4 of 366 company-years from 2011 to 2025; of the 4 that held and could be read a year later, 0 still held.
analytics.note: Class: every filer in SEC's annual frames whose revenue in the test's base year was at least $100.00B (half the company's newest revenue, rounded down to 1, 2 or 5 times a power of ten) Each year t is a calendar-year frame: SEC places in it, for each filer, the fiscal year that best fits the calendar year; t-1 is the frame a year earlier, and the two periods must end a whole number of years apart. Frames carry no filing date: a value restated later is the restated value. The company itself is not counted: the rate is of the other filers of the class, and the years in which the test held for the company are listed apart. A filer in the class in the base year with no value in year t (it was bought, went under, stopped filing, or changed its tags) is in the class but not computable: the rate is of the filers that can still be read. A parent and a subsidiary that both file are two filers; a filer that reports in another currency is in no USD frame. The SIC code is the filer's code today, not the code it had in year t.

analytics.label: Enterprise value
analytics.reading: Market value $5.50T plus total debt $33.37B less cash and marketable securities $56.59B (2026-07-26) is $5.48T.
analytics.note: Enterprise value = market value + total debt − cash and marketable securities (leases, preferred stock and minority interests are left out). Both balances are of the newest balance sheet filed by the price's date; one last reported for an older date is not carried forward. Non-current marketable securities are not subtracted: for a company that holds a long-dated portfolio the enterprise value here is higher than one that counts it.

analytics.label: Revenue growth the price implies (reverse DCF)
analytics.formula: PV(g) = enterprise value $5.48T, solved for g between −50% and +100%
analytics.reading: At these assumptions the enterprise value of $5.48T needs revenue to grow 13.4% a year for 10 years, from $302.97B to $1.07T. The company's own revenue grew +100.0% a year over its last three fiscal years. The largest revenue any filer reported for 2025 is $716.92B (AMAZON.COM, INC.): the implied year-10 revenue is 1.5 times that. Of 40 ten-year spans of filers that started at its size (revenue of $151.48B to $605.94B; starts 2009 to 2015), 0 grew at least that fast (median 1.3% a year, 90th percentile 8.0%; 4 more could not be followed for ten years). With the operating margin at the industry's median of 4.2% (n = 61, 2025) instead of 65.2%, no growth from −50% to +100% a year reaches the price. With the operating margin at the industry's 90th percentile of 26.6% (n = 61, 2025) instead of 65.2%, the same price needs 28.1% a year. Across the grid (discount rate ±2 points, margin ±5 points) the implied growth runs from 6.5% to 19.7% a year (15 of 15 cells solve).
analytics.note: Arithmetic under stated assumptions, not a forecast and not advice: it says what constant growth the price would need if every assumption below held. Starting revenue $302.97B (Revenue, four quarters ended 2026-07-26). Operating margin 65.2%, every year: the trailing operating margin, $197.58B ÷ $302.97B. Tax on operating profit 21% (the US federal rate, a stated default). Sales-to-capital 1.47: trailing revenue $302.97B ÷ invested capital $205.76B (equity $228.98B + debt $33.37B − cash and securities $56.59B, 2026-07-26); each dollar of new revenue is assumed to need capital at this ratio. Discount rate 9% a year (a stated default, near a long-run US equity return). After 10 years, growth of 3% a year forever. Cash flow = revenue × margin × (1 − tax) − (revenue − last year's revenue) ÷ sales-to-capital; discounted at the end of each year; compared with the enterprise value.

analytics.note: The target is above the model's value at every growth from -50% to 100% a year. Operating margin 4.2%: the median of the 61 other SIC 3674 filers with revenue of at least $100.0M with an operating margin in 2025 (SEC frames); every other assumption unchanged.
